findings.Quote:
His face hadn't changed since she arrived — not surprised, not relieved, not visibly working anything out. The face of a man who'd made his choices a long time ago and wasn't going back over them.

She didn't know what he meant. She didn't have time to ask.
findings.Note: CJ reacts to Nzambe's face as if he'd said something ('what he meant'), but no dialogue or line preceded this — the referent is missing, breaking sense continuity
findings.Fix: give Nzambe a short ambiguous line before this, or change 'what he meant' to 'what he was thinking'

findings.Quote: Pip went to the buried spot. He'd been patient through all of it — the burial, the descent, the leaving — and now he did what he did at every stop that mattered. He sniffed the sealed patch of asphalt, thorough, starting at one
findings.Note: Purpose calls for Pip trotting to the nearest tine and lifting his leg on the machine itself, with the machine's non-reaction as the joke; instead the excerpt has him investigating the buried spot on the ground, and the beat cuts off before the leg-lift or the machine's reaction appear at all.
findings.Fix: Redirect Pip to the nearest tine as specified, include the leg-lift, and show the machine's indifference to complete the comedic beat.

findings.Quote: There was a word for what Pip had just done. He didn't use it. It would have been either too small or too big, and he wasn't sure which.
findings.Note: Coy withholding-the-word device reads as a writerly trick rather than character insight; tells us Wes is moved without showing it.
findings.Fix: Cut the meta-commentary and let the observed action (Pip sitting, the wail changing register) carry the weight, or give the actual word and let it land.

findings.Quote: Close enough that six or eight didn't feel like different numbers.
findings.Note: Vague filler phrasing that gestures at danger without specifying anything concrete; reads as padding rather than sensory detail.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete detail (e.g., how the gap looked from his vantage).

findings.Quote: A few years of somebody's budget, lying in the Hillsdale dirt.
findings.Note: Filler-wit aside that editorializes rather than showing; slightly deflates the mechanical tension just built.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with a concrete visual detail (e.g. scorch mark, blinking light) instead of a budget quip.

findings.Quote: Pip was below, in the shadow of the rear stabilizer.
findings.Note: Beat purpose specifies 'Pip does not look up' as a beat, but the prose only places Pip in position without confirming the specified detail of not looking up.
findings.Fix: Add a clause confirming Pip's lack of reaction, e.g. 'Pip didn't look up, didn't break stride.'

findings.Quote: the kind of loud that tears the throat
findings.Note: Stock intensifier phrasing for shouting effort.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a more specific physical detail, e.g. 'loud enough that his voice cracked.'

findings.Quote: A hundred feet. That was the problem.
findings.Note: Short declarative aphorism-style filler that states the obvious rather than dramatizing the distance.
findings.Fix: Fold the distance into the action directly rather than isolating it as a stated 'problem.'

findings.Quote: Smart, if it was. He didn't know enough about ArcSec drone doctrine to say.
findings.Note: Hedging aside reads as filler commentary rather than advancing tension or characterization.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence; let the observation stand without the self-aware qualifier.

findings.Quote: the hull a drum under him
findings.Note: Repeated metaphor (also appears earlier in the manuscript pattern) trending toward stock imagery for rhythmic machine sound.
findings.Fix: Vary the metaphor or cut for plainer description.

findings.Quote: the loose full commitment of a dog
findings.Note: vague abstraction stands in for the concrete image the sentence is trying to earn; reads as filler generalization rather than observed detail
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a specific physical beat

findings.Quote: the kind of dog that looks put together specifically to be hard to stop once it has somewhere to be
findings.Note: cute overwritten aphorism about the dog's build, tips into whimsy that undercuts the grounded tone
findings.Fix: trim to a plainer physical description

findings.Quote: the way you let yourself be lifted when you've been moving forty miles and your body has said everything it has to say
findings.Note: the 'body has said everything it has to say' is a soft, worn personification standing in for exhaustion
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical detail (trembling legs, slack weight) instead of the abstraction

findings.Quote: Gently. The way you pick something up when you know exactly what it weighs and have learned to respect the weight.
findings.Note: aphoristic phrasing that explains the gesture instead of trusting the preceding image; slightly overwritten repetition of 'weight'
findings.Fix: cut second sentence, let 'Gently' stand alone or replace with a sharper concrete beat

findings.Quote: like someone in a room where they don't want to make a sound
findings.Note: generic simile that tells rather than shows Wes's tension, slightly deflates the tautness of the scene
findings.Fix: replace with a specific physical detail of Wes's posture or breath

findings.Quote: Read it, she told herself. Whatever it's doing to that module, get it all — the depth, the interval, the sequence — get enough that somebody downstream can make sense of it.
findings.Note: Internal-monologue exposition that tells us her professionalism/purpose rather than showing it through the observation itself; slows the procedural tension with a explainer aside.
findings.Fix: Cut to the direct observation and let the itemized data (depth, interval, sequence) appear as her actual notation, not a self-directed pep talk.

findings.Quote: a hundred miles of the same signal, carried through drone strikes and threat-wails and scav camps and the flat Illinois distance, and in all of it nothing had ever once answered back
findings.Note: This is a reflective, almost eulogistic aside that pulls against the beat's stated flatness/dormancy and CJ's wordless witnessing — it editorializes rather than holding record.
findings.Fix: Trim to the concrete fact (the interval held for a hundred miles) and cut the summary emotional framing.

findings.Quote: The sounds it made now were the sounds of a long work c
findings.Note: Sentence is cut off / incomplete, breaking the read entirely.
findings.Fix: Complete the sentence or cut it.

findings.Quote: His parents, who still didn't know where he was.
findings.Note: Stock guilt-beat tacked onto the horizon-gazing montage, a shorthand emotional cue rather than earned detail.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with something more specific to Wes's situation.

findings.Quote: He'd been patient through all of it — the burial, the descent, the leaving — and now he did what he did at every stop that mattered.
findings.Note: Tells us Pip's meaningfulness/ritual instead of letting the deflating comedy of the leg-lift land on its own; undercuts the beat's stated comic-after-sacred timing by pre-explaining the dog's significance.
findings.Fix: Cut the editorializing clause and go straight to the action: 'Pip went to the buried spot and sniffed the sealed patch of asphalt, thorough, starting at one—'
